description: C4 suite release manifest — maps suite versions to component versions

1.0.18.notes: Verification patch; IDs are unchanged. Eight defects where c4 trusted metadata or stored names instead of rechecking bytes, found while dogfooding c4 to sync live state between two machines. (1) c4 diff <c4m> <dir> trusted size+mtime, so a corrupted copy that kept both reported no differences; the directory side is now always hashed. (2) Scans now settle racy files (git's racy rule), so a same-size rewrite within the second a scan saw a file is never recorded with stale content. (3) c4 patch hashes content as it copies from the store or a --source directory and refuses bytes that do not match their ID, leaving the destination untouched; it now exits 1 when any operation fails. (4) c4 cat verifies an object before printing it. (5) Stores written on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS) are readable on Linux. (6) c4 patch restores nested directory times, so c4 id after a sync matches the target. (7) c4 diff | c4 paths lists changed paths. (8) Malformed c4m exits 1 instead of panicking. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep from their 1.0.17 code.

1.0.17.notes: Correctness and safety patch; IDs are unchanged. (1) c4 id -s re-serialized any file whose content parsed as c4m, so the store held different bytes than the disk and the original was unrecoverable (#43); files are now stored exactly as read and c4 cat returns stored bytes verbatim. Trees containing c4m files snapshotted with <= 1.0.16 should be re-snapshotted. (2) c4 patch <c4m> <dir> followed symbolic links already in the destination and could write outside it; every write is now confined to the destination and refused through a link. (3) Scanning a symlink cycle (up -> ..) crashed with a stack overflow; the link now gets a null ID. (4) -S snapshots now store the folded ID-list object (#45); patch still cannot expand folded entries and refuses them as in 1.0.16 instead of writing the ID list as a file. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep from their 1.0.16 code.

1.0.16.notes: Correctness patch: three defects found by adversarial review of the shipped binary. (1) Durability ordering — batch-mode store objects were renamed to their final hash names before the end-of-command device barrier, so a power cut could leave a torn object at a valid name that a later run's write-skip would adopt silently; objects now publish only after the barrier, so presence at a hash name always implies bytes on stable media. (2) c4 log resolved the whole patch chain from scratch per section (super-quadratic; 1000 sections did not finish) — now resolves incrementally (1000 sections ~5s). (3) With sequence folding (-S), stored snapshots silently contained none of their frames because folded pattern names are not files; folded entries now expand to their members at store time. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.15.notes: Same-day supersede of 1.0.14 (which shipped with a Windows defect: the batch durability barrier fsync'd directory handles, which Windows refuses — spurious 'Access is denied' warnings on every c4 id -s / c4 patch and four failing store tests; no data loss). The barrier now routes through a platform-conditional store.SyncDir (no-op on Windows, F_FULLFSYNC on darwin, directory fsync elsewhere), verified on real Windows hardware. Also restores Go 1.16 buildability (legacy build-tag pairs, 1.16-compatible test code). Otherwise identical to 1.0.14: guided-scan directory-ID corruption fix (regenerate c4m files made with c4 id --continue on ≤1.0.13), bottom-up dir IDs (O(2^depth) → O(N)), path-keyed diff, null-timestamp rendering, safety defaults (pre-state capture with verbatim revert, protected paths, self-capturing snapshots), and the batch-barrier durability default with no flags (ingest ~180s → ~4.3s, materialize ~171s → ~4.4s on a 20k-file tree).

1.0.14.notes: SUPERSEDED same-day by 1.0.15 (Windows batch-barrier fix). Correctness/safety/perf patch. CRITICAL: c4m files produced by guided scans (c4 id --continue) on ≤1.0.13 have wrong directory IDs (the empty-input ID was written for every directory entry) and should be regenerated; file IDs were unaffected. Directory C4 IDs are now computed bottom-up, which also fixes O(2^depth) deep-tree scans (~93s → ~0.007s at depth 20). c4m.Diff keys entries by full path. Null timestamps render as - in structure mode. Safety defaults: c4 patch reconcile forms capture the destination's pre-state durably before applying and print a verbatim revert command; protected-path support closes a data-loss hazard (an unguarded patch could delete .git); snapshots are self-capturing (c4 cat <id> reproduces the manifest from the store alone). Performance: snapshot ingest ~180s → ~4.3s and materialize ~171s → ~4.4s on a 20k-file/105MB tree via the batch durability barrier — now the only durability behavior; the --no-fsync/--durable flags are removed. c4 gc (never released) was withdrawn before shipping. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.13.notes: Scan performance: O(D × N) propagateMetadata replaced with single-pass depth-stack (5.14M-entry trees went from 16-20 min hang to 2m 24s). Plus six API additions in c4: c4m.PropagateMetadata exported, c4m.WriteCanonical, scan.WithProgress, scan.WithMaxConcurrency, scan.WithContext, scan.WithEntryStream; progressive scanner propagation wired.

1.0.12.notes: Version bump to 1.0.12 across all components.

1.0.11.notes: Version bump to 1.0.11 across all components.

1.0.10.notes: Version alignment across all components. c4ts and c4-swift brought to 1.0.10.

1.0.6.notes: Initial coordinated release. TypeScript and Swift implementations, c4sh UX improvements, scan-everything fix.

1.0.19.notes: Patch. c4m canonical order: digit runs compare as integers of any length, never through a 64-bit or double parse, so a tree whose names hold runs of 20 or more digits has one ID instead of one per run (c4 Go, c4ts, c4-swift fixed; c4py was already right); text segments compare whole, a1 < ab (libc4 fixed). Shared vectors c4m/testdata/natural_sort_vectors.json in every implementation. Names with runs of 18 digits or fewer sort exactly as before, so their IDs are unchanged. Also c4git: the smudge filter passed through only the first 256 bytes of a non-pointer blob (data loss on checkout), fixed. c4-containers: README names C4_S3_ENDPOINT; s3worker passes S3_ENDPOINT through. Other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.20.status: planned: cut once c4-operator v0.2.0 is published

c4-farm.note: the farm CLI; c4 farm ... runs it. Pinned to the c4-operator tag the suite was tested with; c4-operator pins c4 in its go.mod the other way. Taken from the c4-operator GitHub release (goreleaser archive, with the tool locks the release workflow embeds), not rebuilt from source

c4-agent.note: the host runner; macOS and Linux only. Taken from the c4-operator GitHub release (goreleaser archive, with the tool locks the release workflow embeds), not rebuilt from source

c4-unit.note: the unit runner c4-agent runs its units with; in the archives beside c4-agent (the c4-agent formula carries it on Homebrew)

1.0.20.notes: Patch. c4: `c4 <name>` runs `c4-<name>` from PATH when no file or directory of that name exists, and `c4 help` lists the installed tools; nothing that works on 1.0.19 changes meaning. The suite archives and the Homebrew formula now bring the farm tools from c4-operator v0.2.0: c4-farm (all platforms), c4-agent and c4-unit (c4-agent on macOS and Linux), taken from that release's own archives; `brew install mrjoshuak/tap/c4` installs c4, c4sh, c4git and, through the tap's c4-farm and c4-agent formulas, `c4 farm`. Other components ship version-lockstep.
